frequency_question: How often do major comprehensive energy/permitting reform omnibus packages successfully pass both chambers and get signed into law within a single 2-year congressional session?
membership_rule: Includes major bipartisan or party-line omnibus energy/permitting reform bills explicitly targeting NEPA or pipeline approvals. Excludes minor provisions folded quietly into must-pass appropriations or defense authorization bills unless they carried standalone comprehensive permitting reform titles.

cases.name: Energy Infrastructure Act / IIJA Permitting Provisions
Manchin Permitting Reform Bill (Energy Independence and Security Act attempts)
Fiscal Responsibility Act Permitting Provisions (NEPA reform)

coverage_note: 5 major distinct legislative pushes for comprehensive energy permitting reform in modern polarized Congresses; 2 succeeded (often attached to broader must-pass vehicles like infrastructure or debt ceiling deals).
known_gaps: Excludes smaller standalone pipeline riders that were successfully attached to NDAA or Omnibus bills without being termed 'comprehensive energy permitting reform'.
validity_reason: Valid through the current polarization regime and Senate filibuster rules, which reset or potentially evolve at the start of each new Congress.
